paper_title: AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Video diffusion transformers generate high-quality videos, but the quadratic cost of 3D full attention dominates their inference. Dynamic block-sparse attention reduces this cost by computing exact attention only on key/value blocks selected from current activations. However, its fidelity degrades under aggressive sparsity: blocks are scored from coarse summaries or formed by costly global clustering, pruned blocks vanish from the softmax, and whole tiles are kept or dropped even when only a few of their keys matter. To address these limitations, we propose Accurate Block Attention (AB-Attention), a training-free method that accurately approximates dense attention at high sparsity. Its Intra-Block Clustering Selector (IBCS) estimates block importance faithfully yet cheaply by clustering queries only within each query block, without permuting tokens. Sampling with Inclusion-Probability Weighting (SIP) then samples blocks in proportion to these estimates and reweights them by inverse inclusion probability, so that one pass estimates dense attention rather than truncating it. Finally, its kernel gathers key/value blocks much smaller than a tile into full tensor-core tiles, refining selection at no extra tensor-core cost. On Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo, AB-Attention skips 89--92\% of attention, whereas the baselines compute 1.8--3.6$\times$ as much, yet it still improves PSNR by up to 4.4~dB over the strongest baseline and achieves up to 2.23$\times$ end-to-end speedup. Our code is available at https://github.com/InfRec-Cardinal/AB-Attention.

Introduction Video diffusion transformers [1, 2] primarily rely on 3D full attention to capture spatial and temporal dependencies, enabling high-quality generation. However, the computational cost of full attention grows quadratically with the sequence length. As the video resolution and number of frames increase, attention becomes increasingly expensive. Since this computation is repeated across transformer layers and denoising steps, attention has long been major inference bottleneck [3, 4]. Reducing the cost of attention while preserving generation quality is therefore essential for generating longer and higher-resolution videos. Sparse attention reduces this cost by computing only subset of querykey pairs. Early methods apply predefined spatial or temporal patterns, such as local 3D windows [4], energy-decay masks [5], or per-head spatial and temporal masks [3]. These predefined layouts reduce the need for online block scoring, but their limited adaptability to attention variations across prompts, heads, and denoising steps can require retaining many unimportant pairs to preserve important interactions. Dynamic methods instead select key/value blocks from the current activations, adapting the sparsity pattern to the input at the cost of online scoring. Since block-sparse kernels execute attention in fixed-size tiles, they partition queries and keys into tile-aligned blocks, estimate block importance cheaply from mean-pooled tokens [6] or antidiagonal attention samples [7], and compute exact attention only on the most important blocks. SVG2 [8] instead forms the blocks by clustering and permuting tokens. Despite this progress, dynamic methods remain limited by three design choices: 1) Importance estimates are coarse or costly. Pooling block into one representative mixes tokens with different attention patterns and can misrank blocks, whereas clustering yields faithful representatives only through sequence-wide 𝑘-means and token permutation [8]. 2) Top-𝑘 selection truncates attention. Discarding block removes its contribution from both the attention numerator and the softmax normalizer, which better scores cannot recover. Correction-based methods [911] approximate the discarded remainder, but add separate approximation branch to the exact sparse computation. 3) The selection unit is the execution tile. tile-sized key block is kept or discarded as whole even when only few of its keys matter, and reordering tokens makes blocks more coherent without changing this unit. Finer units need not slow execution, as kernel can gather them into full tiles, but they multiply the candidates to score. We therefore propose Accurate Block Attention (AB-Attention), training-free method that directly addresses these limitations. The Intra-Block Clustering Selector (IBCS) scores key/value blocks with lightweight query clusters formed only within each query block, avoiding costly global clustering and token permutation. Sampling with Inclusion-Probability Weighting (SIP) samples blocks in proportion to these scores and reweights them by inverse inclusion probability. Every block can thus contribute, and single sparse attention pass yields unbiased estimates of both the attention numerator and the softmax normalizer. AB-Attention further performs fine-grained selection with tiled execution: it selects key/value blocks much smaller than an execution tile and gathers them into full tensor-core tiles in its kernel, without reordering any tokens. The sampling plans are reused across few nearby denoising steps, while attention is recomputed at every step [12]. Extensive experiments on representative video diffusion transformers, including Wan2.1 [1] and HunyuanVideo [2], demonstrate that AB-Attention significantly advances the qualityefficiency frontier of training-free sparse attention. It skips 8992% of attention computation, whereas the competing baselines compute 1.83.6 as much, and delivers 1.842.23 end-to-end speedups on single H20 GPU, while achieving the highest fidelity to dense attention and improving PSNR by 1.64.4 dB over the strongest baselines, including SVG2 [8] and DFSAttn [13]. Fine-Grained Selection with Tiled Execution Selection granularity and execution efficiency favor different block sizes. Large key/value blocks align naturally with execution tiles and use tensor cores efficiently, but make selection coarse. Small blocks select important keys more precisely, but are too small to serve as efficient matrix-multiply tiles on their own. AB-Attention co-designs these two levels: it selects small key/value blocks and packs the sampled blocks into full execution tiles. At fixed sampling budget, this preserves the number of tensor-core tile computations while allowing finer-grained selection. For each query block, fused attention kernel gathers its sampled key/value blocks directly into full tiles, applies the inverse-inclusion-probability logit shifts, and performs the usual online softmax and value accumulation in one pass. The kernel gathers sampled blocks by index and packs them on the fly, so noncontiguous blocks require neither token reordering nor materialized reordered sequence. The selector follows the same tiled design. It scores multiple query and key/value blocks in batched matrix operations and aggregates their partial results, avoiding separate operation for every small candidate block. Sampling plans are rebuilt every 𝐶 denoising steps and reused between rebuilds, while attention is recomputed from the current activations at every step. 4. Experiments 4.1. Experimental Setup Models and datasets. We evaluate three text-to-video diffusion transformers: Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B and Wan2.1-T2V-14B [1], and HunyuanVideo-T2V-13B [2]. Every generated video is sampled at 720p resolution and contains 81 frames on Wan2.1 or 129 frames on HunyuanVideo. Text prompts are the 600 prompts of the Penguin Benchmark [2]. Metrics. We compare each sparse video with the corresponding full-attention video from the same prompt and seed and report PSNR, SSIM [17], and LPIPS [18]. To evaluate the videos themselves, independent of the reference, we further report five VBench [19] dimensions: aesthetic quality (AQ), background consistency (BC), imaging quality (IQ), motion smoothness (MS), and subject consistency (SC). Baselines. We compare against three recent state-of-the-art training-free sparse attention methods. RadialAttention [5] applies static energy-decay mask, whereas SVG2 [8] and DFSAttn [13] build their masks dynamically from the current queries and keys. We use the official released code and the default hyperparameters of each baseline, as detailed in Appendix B.2. The released DFSAttn implementation executes its masks with FlashAttention-2-based block-sparse kernel [20]. For common backend, we execute the masks of all three baselines with FlashInfers FlashAttention-3 block-sparse backend [21]; this is also the backend used by the released RadialAttention and SVG2 implementations. Implementation details. Each video is generated on NVIDIA H20 GPUs in BF16 precision with PyTorch 2.6 and CUDA 12.4. Dense attention, including the dense steps of every method, uses FlashAttention-3 [22]. Following prior work [5, 13], all methods keep attention dense in the first transformer block and during the first 10 of the 50 denoising steps. AB-Attention uses key/value block size of 4, query block size of 128, and eight query clusters per query block, and rebuilds its sampling plan every four denoising steps. Its sampling budget is kept fixed for each model, resulting in an 89.16% sparsity on both Wan2.1 models and 92.35% on HunyuanVideo. End-to-end latency is measured following the protocol in Appendix C. 4.2. Main Results Table 1 reports the quality and efficiency of every method on all three models. AB-Attention attains the best PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS of any method on every model and consistently improves PSNR over the strongest baseline by 1.64.4 dB. It does so while skipping 8992% of attention computation, more than any baseline: every competing baseline computes 1.83.6 times as much attention. Figures 1 and 4 show the same effect visually: AB-Attention stays close to the dense reference where the baselines lose fine detail. On VBench, AB-Attention remains close to dense attention on all five dimensions, showing that the videos it generates retain their overall visual quality. 8 AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers Figure 4 Qualitative comparison on Wan2.1-T2V-14B. Panels (a)(d) are four Penguin Benchmark prompts, abbreviated with ellipses. Within panel, rows are methods and columns are frames 12, 40, and 68 of the same video. Headers show sparsity and full-video PSNR relative to the dense reference. 9 AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers Table 2 Ablation of the AB-Attention components on Wan2.1-T2V-14B. Each variant replaces one component at the same 89.16% sparsity. Variant PSNR SSIM LPIPS AB-Attention 29.705 0.9154 0. IBCS Query pooling 28.793 0.91 0.9024 0.1112 SIP w/o weights 25.706 4.00 0.8427 0.1911 Uniform w/o weights 22.452 7.25 0.7437 0.4749 25.711 3.99 0.8420 0.1996 Top-𝑘 selection Tiling Tile-level selection 28.686 1.02 0.9006 0. Figure 5 PSNR versus selection block size on Wan2.1-T2V-14B. Efficiency follows the same ordering. AB-Attention reaches end-to-end speedups of 1.842.23, ahead of every baseline on every model, and cuts the generation time of HunyuanVideo video from 4399 to 1975 s. Its closest competitor, DFSAttn on HunyuanVideo, reaches 2.07 only while computing 2.4 times as much attention, 18.71% versus 7.65% of dense attention. AB-Attention is thus at once the sparsest, the most faithful, and the fastest method on every model in Table 1. 4.3. Ablation Study Table 2 ablates the three core designs of AB-Attention one at time, keeping the other two fixed: the query clusters of IBCS, the sampling and weighting of SIP, and the fine-grained key/value selection unit. All variants use Wan2.1-T2V-14B with 100 prompts randomly sampled from the 600 Penguin Benchmark prompts and run at the same 89.16% sparsity as the main results. Query clustering. IBCS summarizes each query block with its eight query clusters. To test whether grouping queries by feature similarity matters, we instead average eight consecutive 16-query intervals, as in positional sub-block pooling [13], keeping the number of representatives and hence the overall scoring cost unchanged. This query pooling variant lowers PSNR by 0.91 dB, with SSIM and LPIPS degrading accordingly. positional interval mixes queries that attend to different keys, so its single mean can underrate key block that only some of them attend to, whereas cluster gathers queries with similar features, which tend to attend to similar keys. Sampling and weighting. We compare SIP with three simpler alternatives at the same budget: scoreproportional sampling without the inverse-inclusion weights, uniform sampling without weights, and deterministic top-𝑘 selection. Removing the weights lowers PSNR by 4.00 dB, to the level of top-𝑘 selection: without them, the blocks outside the sample are simply dropped, and sampling becomes another form of pruning. Discarding the scores as well then costs further 3.25 dB and more than doubles LPIPS, because uniform sampling spends most of its fixed budget on the many blocks that receive little attention, as Figure 2(a) shows. The scores thus decide where to spend the limited budget, and the weights account for the blocks it leaves out; SIP needs both. Selection granularity. Tile-level selection, which scores and samples whole execution tiles as conventional block-sparse attention does, lowers PSNR by 1.02 dB. As Figure 5 shows, PSNR rises steadily as the selection block shrinks from full tile toward the 4-token blocks of AB-Attention, and Appendix shows the same trend for SSIM and LPIPS. Smaller key/value blocks let the sample keep the few important keys in region without spending any budget on their neighbors, and since the kernel of Section 3.3 packs them into full tiles, this gain costs no extra tensor-core work. 10 AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers Overall, replacing SIP costs by far the most, 3.997.25 dB of PSNR, followed by tile-level selection at 1.02 dB and query pooling at 0.91 dB. Every variant is worse than AB-Attention on all three metrics, so at the same budget each component of AB-Attention contributes to its fidelity. 5. Related Work Sparse Attention. Sparse attention accelerates video diffusion transformers [2325] by restricting querykey interactions to subset that can be computed efficiently [2631]. Static methods exploit video geometry with fixed sparsity patterns [32]: Sliding Tile Attention [4] uses tiled local 3D windows, Radial Attention [5] constructs static multiscale mask from spatiotemporal energy decay, and Sparse VideoGen [3] profiles attention heads online to assign each head predefined spatial or temporal pattern. Dynamic methods instead infer sparsity from the current activations. XAttention [7] estimates block importance by summing attention scores along strided antidiagonals, and SpargeAttention [6] combines coarse prediction from mean-compressed self-similar blocks with softmax-aware filtering. To improve block representations, SVG2 [8] clusters tokens by semantic similarity with 𝑘-means and permutes each cluster into contiguous blocks, and DFSAttn [13] combines 3D Hilbert-curve reordering with hierarchical sub-block scoring. SPADE [33] adapts block summaries and sparsity policies to each input. AdaSpa [12] and RAPID [34] amortize sparsity search by reusing and adapting masks across denoising steps. Across these designs, selection granularity, grouping overhead, and hardware-friendly execution remain coupled. Correction-Based Sparse Attention. Pruning removes the skipped interactions from the attention numerator and the softmax normalizer. Training-free correction methods approximate these missing contributions: Rectified SpaAttn [9] rectifies the amplified weights of retained blocks and recovers those of pruned blocks from pooled attention, PISA [10] approximates the remaining blocks with block-wise Taylor expansion, and SVG-EAR [11] compensates pruned blocks with cluster centroids and routes exact computation to the blocks with the largest error. All three compute selected blocks exactly and approximate the rest, whereas AB-Attention estimates both the numerator and the normalizer from one weighted sample of all blocks. Other Acceleration Methods. Diffusion inference can also be accelerated by reducing denoising steps [3539], reusing intermediate computation [4042], or reducing the sequence length processed per step [43, 44]. Fast solvers such as DPM-Solver [45] reduce the number of model evaluations, while progressive distillation [46] repeatedly trains student to halve the number of sampling steps. TeaCache [47] reuses cached model outputs across denoising steps while the accumulated difference of timestep-modulated inputs stays below threshold. DyDiT [48] dynamically adjusts model width across denoising timesteps and skips computation for less important spatial tokens; DyDiT++ [49] extends this approach to video generation and other visual-generation settings. RAPID3 [50] jointly learns policies for denoising-step skipping, feature-cache reuse, and sparseattention selection. FlashAttention [14] reduces memory traffic by computing exact attention tile by tile in on-chip memory, and SageAttention [51] accelerates attention by quantizing queries and keys to INT8. These approaches are complementary to sparse attention and can be combined with it [22, 52]. 6. Conclusion We presented AB-Attention, training-free sparse attention method for video diffusion transformers that directly estimates dense attention rather than truncating it. IBCS scores key/value blocks with lightweight query clusters formed only within each query block, and SIP samples blocks in proportion 11 AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers to these scores and reweights them by their inverse inclusion probabilities, so that single blocksparse pass yields unbiased estimates of the attention numerator and normalizer. AB-Attention further decouples selection from execution: it selects key/value blocks much smaller than tile and packs them into full tensor-core tiles in its kernel. On both Wan2.1 and HunyuanVideo, AB-Attention skips 8992% of attention, whereas the baselines compute 1.83.6 as much, yet it stays closest to dense attention and reaches the highest end-to-end speedups of 1.842.23. Limitations and future work. Despite these encouraging results, AB-Attention remains limited in both its current implementation and application scope. Our kernel is built for the H20 GPUs used in our experiments and currently supports only forward inference, while our evaluation covers three text-to-video diffusion transformers. Future work will address these limitations through kernel support for further hardware, evaluation on broader range of models, and trainable implementation with backward support that enables fine-tuning under AB-Attention. 12 AB-Attention: Accurate Block Attention for Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers
